title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations (estimand=paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate)
abstract: Estimand and scope (first sentence): This preregistered study (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) tests a single, precise estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (i.e., each pair reuses one canonical LLM candidate that is scored identically by a deterministic validator). Motivation: intent→configuration generation for NetOps must be judged by deterministic semantic validators (reachability/ACL/routing checks) to be operationally meaningful. Method and artifacts: we generated N=120 template‑aligned intent→config tasks, produced one canonical LLM candidate per task using the declared model gpt‑5‑mini, and scored each canonical candidate under two conditions (baseline template and guarded LLM condition) with deterministic_netops_validator_v5; all execution and scoring artifacts and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints are published in the submission bundle. Key quantitative result (artifact‑grounded): baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared_initial seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Main interpretation: the preregistered confirmatory design correctly tests verifier‑consistency for identical inputs but does not estimate independent LLM generative reliability; we diagnose why (archived canonical candidates + deterministic validator) and present artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question practitioners typically need.

sections.introduction:
Problem and operational stake. Translating high‑level operator intent into low‑level device configuration is a routine NetOps task whose correctness is safety‑critical: incorrect steps can break reachability, violate ACLs, or create unsafe transient states during multi‑step changes. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) are the accepted operational oracle for pre‑deployment checks (see Brown et al., Batfish evolution [10.1145/3603269.3604866]). Generative LLMs promise rapid intent→config production but raise questions about reliability when judged by deterministic validators.
Research question and preregistered estimand. After a fresh literature scan and preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...), we selected the confirmatory estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (each task uses a single canonical LLM candidate reused across scoring conditions). This estimand answers whether a deterministic validator yields different pass/fail decisions when identical artifacts are presented under two labeled conditions. It does not—by design—estimate the probability that independently sampled LLM outputs will pass the validator; that is a different, operational estimand we describe below and make runnable from our artifact bundle.
Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment and release of exhaustive execution and scoring traces (per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints included). (2) Exact, archived confirmatory results and deterministic reconciliation showing baseline = 120/120 and guarded = 120/120 verifier passes (paired difference 0.00). (3) An artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory contrast collapsed and a runnable, deterministic plan to answer the independent generative‑reliability question without losing reproducibility.
sections.related_work:
Verifier‑grounded NetOps and generate–validate–repair. Offline validators such as Batfish and successors provide deterministic reachability and policy checks that form the operational safety oracle for network changes [10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Contemporary LLM→NetOps work typically couples generation with deterministic verification and bounded repair loops; empirical studies differ in sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs. independent samples), repair budgets, and validator scope. Prior work emphasizing iterative repair budgets finds most gains in early iterations and shows that orchestration often dominates raw model choice (see iterative repair literature in the evidence bundle).
Methodological axes in prior evaluations. Important methodological contrasts are: (A) sampling semantics—shared canonical candidates vs. independent per‑condition seeds; (B) repair budgets and loop rules; and (C) validator scope (syntactic parsing vs. full semantic verification). These choices materially affect measured reliability. Our preregistered shared_initial_candidate design isolates validator determinism but cannot inform about independent generative variance; we make this distinction explicit and provide the artifacts required to replay either paradigm reliably.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, task bank, and frozen design. The study was preregistered as CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 prior to any model calls (SHA‑256 7db1663c...). The design specified: N=120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, one canonical LLM call per task (seed_0), deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and the exact analysis plan (paired_binary_analysis_v1 with 10,000 bootstrap replicates, seed = 1729). All source artifacts (task generator, seeds, model configuration, provider traces, scoring traces) are archived in the submission bundle with per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints (see execution/execution_manifest.json).
Task synthesis and verifier coupling. Tasks were programmatically synthesized from an explicit template bank (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (ordered minimal operations required by intent), workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty annotation (changed_interface_count, transient_rule_count). The deterministic validator enforces those workflow_policies and emits structured JSON traces per episode (execution/scoring/*.json).
Generation and scoring pipeline (artifact links). Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). For the confirmatory run we generated a single canonical candidate per task that was reused for both scoring conditions; canonical responses are archived at execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt (example SHA‑256s: task‑000001 8f38c8be..., task‑000002 ae967f70..., task‑000003 f7f4db24...). Each candidate was scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per‑episode scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/*.json (example execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...).
Short mapping (required revision from peer review). The table below concisely contrasts the operational question practitioners typically need, the preregistered estimand we tested, and the causal reason the confirmatory design produced a degenerate paired contingency. The artifacts that support each mapping entry are cited by exact paths and SHA‑256s.

Mapping (operational question vs. preregistered estimand vs. causal reason)

- Operational question practitioners need: "Independent generative reliability" — i.e., P(LLM_candidate passes validator) under independent sampling. (How to run from our bundle: perform independent_per_condition rerun; see Runnable modifications section.)
- Preregistered estimand tested here: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline with generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (single canonical candidate generated per task and reused across scoring conditions). (Preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...; model config SHA‑256 a40e96e2...)
- Causal reason confirmatory contrast collapsed: identical canonical candidate files were reused across conditions (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt, e.g., task-000001 SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), and the validator is deterministic (execution/scoring/*.json shows identical parsed_command_count/validation_after.valid for both episodes), so identical inputs produce identical deterministic outputs (paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...).

Representative validator trace excerpt (artifact‑grounded example). The per‑episode scoring JSON for task‑000001 (execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...) contains the deterministic validator fields used in our adjudication. Excerpted, verbatim fields from that archived trace: parsed_command_count = 4; required_command_count = 4; normalized_configuration = "interface edge1 admin down\ninterface edge1 vlan 30\ninterface edge1 mtu 1600\ninterface edge1 admin up"; validation_after.valid = true. These exact values are published in the bundle and permit byte‑for‑byte reruns of the scoring step.

Analysis plan and execution accounting. The preregistered primary analysis was paired_binary_analysis_v1: compute the per‑pair difference guarded_i − baseline_i and report the mean and a 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Execution accounting (execution/execution_manifest.json) shows planned_episode_count = 240, completed_episode_count = 240, model_calls_used = 120 (one canonical generation per pair), failed_episode_count = 0. The analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 9c77c96f..., paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...) are included in the bundle.
sections.results:
Confirmatory numerical outcome (artifact‑grounded). All preregistered episodes completed. Baseline_success_count = 120/120; Guarded_success_count (gpt‑5‑mini with shared_initial seed_0) = 120/120. The paired contingency is degenerate: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). The primary paired estimator = 0.00. Bootstrap (10,000) percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap seed = 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All these values are reproduced exactly in analysis/results.json and supporting CSVs included in the artifact bundle.
Why the confirmatory statistics are correct but limited in operational interpretation. The confirmatory test faithfully estimates its preregistered estimand—whether a deterministic validator produces different pass/fail outcomes when identical canonical artifacts are presented under two labels. The result (no difference) follows deterministically from the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics plus a deterministic validator. However, this outcome does not address the operational question of independent LLM generative reliability (the probability that independently sampled LLM candidates pass the validator), which requires independent sampling semantics (separate seeds per condition) or multi‑seed replication.
Diagnostics visible in the archive. The execution and scoring artifacts explicitly demonstrate the causal chain: (1) canonical candidate files for each pair are identical across conditions (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; example task‑000001 SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), (2) the validator JSON traces show identical parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, and validation_after.valid = true for both baseline and guarded episodes (execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), and (3) the paired contingency file analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv records the degenerate counts (SHA‑256 9f25790c...). These artifacts permit byte‑for‑byte audit and deterministic reruns.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational recommendation. The preregistered confirmatory run performed exactly as specified and the reported statistics are correct for the preregistered estimand. Practitioners, however, usually need independent per‑condition generative reliability—P(LLM_candidate passes validator) under independent sampling—because deployment reliability depends on stochasticity in generation. To support that question while preserving reproducibility, we provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications that can be executed deterministically using the published bundle: (A) independent_per_condition confirmatory rerun: generate distinct seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore using deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and compute paired contrasts; (B) multi‑seed design: K≥3 independent seeds per condition per task to estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification: run an independent second validator and report intersection/union pass rates to reduce validator–task coupling. All required artifacts and call traces to run these reruns are included in the submission bundle (execution/provider_calls/*.json, execution/call_cache/*, execution/task_manifest.jsonl).
Threats to validity (artifact‑identified). Internal validity: the shared_initial design intentionally removed generation variance and therefore cannot adjudicate independent generative reliability. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks and a single deterministic validator can overstate success relative to open natural language intents. External validity: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic templates limit generalization. Conclusion validity: a degenerate contingency yields trivial inferential outputs that are technically correct but uninformative about the deployment reliability practitioners require. All these threats are visible in the archived artifacts and are discussed in the manifest and analysis traces.
Reproducibility and auditability benefits. Publishing exhaustive artifacts (model configuration, provider call traces, canonical candidate files, per‑episode validator JSONs, and full manifest with SHA‑256 fingerprints) transforms ambiguous replication requests into deterministic reruns. For example, the initial master prompt is archived immutably at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e18...). The exact per‑episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) provide the deterministic adjudicator needed to reproduce the confirmatory numbers byte‑for‑byte. This level of artifact completeness is the principal methodological contribution: it clarifies precisely what was tested and permits immediate, deterministic reruns that change only the sampling semantics (not the validator or task definitions) to answer the operational question of interest.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded experiment and released an exhaustive artifact bundle enabling byte‑for‑byte reproduction. Under the preregistered confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate) both baseline and guarded conditions passed the deterministic validator on all N=120 tasks (both 120/120), producing a paired difference of 0.00. The archived artifacts (canonical candidate files and per‑episode validator traces) demonstrate the causal reason: identical inputs plus a deterministic validator necessarily yield identical adjudications. The confirmatory result therefore answers the preregistered estimand (verifier‑consistency for identical inputs) but not the operational question of independent generative reliability. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification) that preserve reproducibility while producing informative independent comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable initial master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
